story.titleZh: 维斯塔潘续约红牛后F1车手市场的下一步走向
story.summaryZh: 马克斯·维斯塔潘与红牛续约至2030年底，这几乎排除了2026年F1前四强车队明年阵容的重大变动，但车手市场仍有一些悬而未决的问题待解决。
story.originalTitle: What's next for F1's driver market after Verstappen's new deal
story.summaryEn: Max Verstappen's recommitment to Red Bull until the end of 2030 has all but ruled out major changes among F1 2026's top four teams next year, but several interesting driver market questions remain unresolved.
detailZh: 随着马克斯·维斯塔潘重新承诺留在红牛直至2030年底，F1车手市场的一大块拼图已经落定。
这几乎排除了明年F1 2026四大车队之间发生重大变动的可能性，但仍有一些耐人寻味的车手市场问题悬而未决。
既然维斯塔潘已决定不进行爆炸性的离开，以下是现在需要解决的主要遗留问题。
红牛的内部选择现在变得更加复杂
既然维斯塔潘（Verstappen）在‘27赛季的位置已经确定，红牛就可以把注意力转向其车队中另外三个席位。伊萨克·哈贾尔（哈贾尔）有望留任，但他的伤病加上利亚姆·劳森（劳森）的替补出场，两者的结合可能会改变这一局面。
不过，小红牛的车手阵容更有可能发生变化。尼古拉·索洛夫（Nikola Tsolov）在二级方程式（Formula 2）中领跑积分榜的表现意味着他正接近被提拔，成为红牛的下一个候补人选，而这可能会带来一个问题。
红牛希望在阿维德·林德布拉德（Arvid Lindblad）强劲的新秀赛季之后将其留在F1，但劳森在另一辆小红牛赛车中的表现表明，他正在做车队需要他做的全部工作。
这意味着，在决定其B队2027年阵容时，红牛很可能必须决定：是想要加速索洛夫的成长，还是继续坚持今年一直表现出色的车手组合。——Edd Straw
阿隆索把自己面临的重大决定推迟了。
费尔南多·阿隆索曾一度看似是车手市场上关键人物之一。
如果他决定这将是自己参赛的最后一个赛季，那么即便阿斯顿·马丁正在经历艰难的2026赛季，2027年也可能会留下一个潜在的有趣席位。
不过，尽管阿隆索在夏休期之前曾公开表示会利用八月来决定自己是否继续参赛，但他度假归来后却把这个问题往后拖了拖。
他说，他脑子里仍需要理清一些事情——好胜心是否还在、是否足以支撑他继续下去——尽管他表示，毫无疑问他肯定会在某个地方继续参赛，无论是F1、达喀尔还是印第500。
但他还耐人寻味地暗示，新合同的推进将取决于车队老板Lawrence Stroll和车队领队Adrian Newey的想法——而他在假期期间一直没有机会见到他们。
要与其中任何一人交谈，只有在F1比赛现场或他下次造访银石工厂时才有机会。
“和Lawrence以及Adrian坐下来谈，如果车队需要我继续开车，我会考虑的，”他说。
“如果我能在另一个位置上更有价值，我会很高兴，我会考虑，而且我也会感到开心。”
一方面，阿隆索的言论暗示存在一些不确定性——无论是对他自己还是对车队来说，接下来会发生什么都还不明朗。
但现实情况更可能是，需要厘清的主要悬念其实是阿斯顿·马丁在2027年能有多强的竞争力。
如果下个赛季的开局和今年一样，你很容易想象阿隆索会认为自己可以不必再全身心投入、再去参加比赛。
但如果本田本周末的升级展现出此前在测功机和匈牙利拍摄日所预示的潜力，并且阿斯顿·马丁能够从其B规格底盘上释放出进一步的改进，那么预计推动这份协议达成的热情会更多一些。
等到阿隆索能够与老斯托尔好好面谈时——最有可能是在银石工厂——赞德沃特站应该已经尘埃落定，阿斯顿·马丁的潜力图景也会更加清晰。
此外，达成协议也没有太大的紧迫性，因为近几个月与这个席位联系在一起的其他潜在大牌车手——如维斯塔潘和塞恩斯——都已在别处确定了自己的未来。
最终，事态的走向指向阿隆索将再次续约。——Jon Noble
阿尔派车队的执行顾问弗拉维奥·布里亚托利几个月前曾半开玩笑地表示，在他弄清楚梅赛德斯将如何处理乔治·拉塞尔和安东内利之前，他不会对皮埃尔·加斯利2027年的队友人选做出决定。
一旦这家德国制造商内部出现爆炸性的矛盾，就有机会趁虚而入、抢下银箭车队的这两位车手——这样的机会实在太诱人，不容错过，尽管其可能性非常渺茫。
但现在这扇门基本上已经关上了，这意味着现任车手科拉平托越来越有可能获得合同续约，只要他继续保持目前的表现。
这位阿根廷车手去年在阿尔派的开局并不稳定，他难以达到外界寄予他的高期望，并在早期经历了不少挫折。
但2025年年底更强劲的表现，以及这股势头延续到了今年，都表明他正在做一切需要做的事情来保住自己的席位。
但基于阿尔派目前在车队的实力排序中所处的位置，以及当下理顺赛车和车队基础设施是首要任务，Colapinto的进步符合他保住席位所需要的水平。
Briatore最近告诉The 比赛，Colapinto“从去年到今年进步了100%”，但他希望看到这种进步继续下去。
所以，如果Colapinto能像现在这样继续下去，完全有理由相信那份合同最终会敲定。
不过，他可能还得再等一段时间才能让事情尘埃落定——因为Briatore最喜欢的就是让他的车手保持饥饿感。- JN
Sharks正在盯上Ocon的哈斯席位
奥康在哈斯的合同中拥有2026年的选择权，但一段时间以来，他一直在朝着出口的方向漂移，手上有多个潜在的备选选项。
不过，他仍然在考虑范围之内，尤其是在8月休赛前表现有所提升之后。
问题在于哈斯车队还有很多其他选择，车队正在耐心地决定谁应该成为奥利·比尔曼的队友，比尔曼拥有2027年的选择权。
双方已达成协议，如果哈斯愿意，可以从迈凯伦租借F2锦标赛领跑者莱昂纳多·福尔纳罗利，今年早些时候他在赫雷斯测试2025款哈斯赛车时给人留下了积极的印象。
目前F2领先者拉斐尔·卡马拉也将很快驾驶这款‘25赛车，他也在人选之中。与他有合约的法拉利正在推动卡马拉获得这个席位。
然而，需要注意的是，法拉利对这个席位并没有直接的控制权。
detailEn: A big piece of the Formula 1 driver market has fallen into place with Max Verstappen's recommitment to Red Bull until the end of 2030.
It's all but ruled out any major changes among F1 2026's top four teams for next year, but there are still some interesting lingering driver market questions.
Here are the major outstanding issues to resolve now that Verstappen's decided not to make a bombshell departure.
Red Bull’s in-house choice is now more complex

Now that Verstappen’s place is certain for ‘27, Red Bull can turn its attention to the other three seats in its stable. Isack Hadjar is on course to remain, but there is the possibility that the combination of his injury and Liam Lawson’s stand-in outing(s) could change that.

However, the Racing Bulls line-up is more likely to change. Nikola Tsolov’s championship-leading performances in Formula 2 mean he’s closing on promotion as Red Bull’s next cab off the rank, which could create a problem.
Red Bull will want to keep Arvid Lindblad in F1 after his strong rookie season, but Lawson’s performances in the other Racing Bulls car means he’s doing exactly the job the team needs him to.

This means that, when it comes to deciding on its B-team’s 2027 line-up, Red Bull will likely have to decide if it wants to accelerate the progress of Tsolov, or stick with a driver line-up that has served it well this year. - Edd Straw
Alonso has deferred his own big decision
Fernando Alonso had appeared at one point to be one of the key players in the driver market.
If he'd decided this was going to be his last season competing, then it could have left – even though Aston Martin is having a difficult 2026 season – a potentially interesting seat open for 2027.

But despite having spoken openly before the summer break of using August to make a call on whether or not he wanted to continue, Alonso has returned from his holidays kicking the can down the road a little bit.

He said he still needed things to be sorted in his own head about whether the competitive drive was still there for him to carry on – even though he says there is no doubt he will be competing somewhere, whether that is F1, Dakar or the Indy 500.

But he also intriguingly suggested that any movement on getting his fresh contract sorted would rest on what team owner Lawrence Stroll and team boss Adrian Newey wanted – and he had not had the chance to see them over the break.
An opportunity for a chat with either would only come at an F1 race or during his next visit to the Silverstone factory.
“Sitting with Lawrence and Adrian, if the need for the team is for me to drive, I will consider,” he said.
“I will be happy if I can be more valuable in another position, I will consider and I will be happy as well.”
On one hand Alonso’s comments suggest that there is some uncertainty – from both himself and the team about what goes on next.
But the reality is probably more that the main ambiguity that needs clearing up is how competitive Aston Martin can be in 2027.
If next season starts like this year did, you could easily see Alonso thinking that he could do without the commitment of going all in and racing again.

But if Honda’s upgrade this weekend shows the promise that has been teased from the dynos and the Hungary filming day, and Aston Martin can unleash further improvements from its B-spec chassis, then expect a tad more enthusiasm to get that deal over the line.
By the time Alonso gets to see Stroll Sr properly, most likely at the Silverstone factory, Zandvoort will be in the bag and the picture of Aston Martin’s potential will be clearer.

And there is also no huge rush to get a deal over the line as other potential big-name candidates – like Max Verstappen and Carlos Sainz – linked with the seat over recent months have all locked themselves down elsewhere.
In the end, the direction of travel points towards another contract extension for Alonso. - Jon Noble

Alpine executive advisor Flavio Briatore had cheekily suggested a few months ago that he would hold fire on making a call on who Pierre Gasly’s team-mate in 2027 would be until he knew what Mercedes was doing with George Russell and Kimi Antonelli.
The opportunity to exploit any explosive fall out at the German manufacturer and grab on the Silver Arrows pair was too good a one to miss - even if it was very remote.
But with that door pretty much shut now, it means incumbent Franco Colapinto is increasingly likely to get a contract extension so long as he continues doing what he's doing right now.
The Argentine had a shaky start to life at Alpine last year, as he struggled to meet the high expectations placed on his shoulders and endured his fair share of frustrations early on.
But a stronger end to 2025, and with momentum having carried through into this year, has pointed to him doing everything he needs to stay.

But based on where Alpine is in the pecking order, and that sorting out its car and team infrastructure right now is the main priority, Colapinto’s progress is in line with what is needed for him to keep his seat.
Briatore told The Race recently that Colapinto was “from last year to this year, improving 100%,” but wanted to see that development continue.
So if Colapinto keeps going like now, there is every reason to believe that deal will get across the line.
He may just have to wait a little bit for things to be settled though - as Briatore likes nothing more than keeping his drivers hungry. - JN
Sharks are circling for Ocon's Haas seat
Esteban Ocon has an option in his Haas contract for 2026, but for some time he’s been drifting towards the exit door with multiple potential alternatives.
However, he’s still in the mix, especially after an improved performance before the August break.
The trouble is that there are many other options for Haas, which is taking a patient approach to deciding who should be team-mate to Ollie Bearman, who is under option for 2027.

An agreement exists to take Formula 2 championship leader Leonardo Fornaroli on loan from McLaren should Haas want to, and he made a positive impression when testing a 2025 Haas at Jerez earlier this year.
Current F2 frontrunner Rafael Camara will also drive the ‘25 car soon and is also in the mix. Ferrari, which has him under contract, is pushing for Camara to get the place.
However, it’s important to note that Ferrari has no direct control over the seat.

relatedItems.titleZh: F1委员会将讨论针对车队的ADUO计划
relatedItems.summaryZh: F1委员会将讨论一项针对车队的ADUO计划，旨在帮助车队摆脱成本上限的困境。
relatedItems.originalTitle: 'ADUO for teams' plan to be discussed by F1
detailZh: 对成本上限规则的全面改革似乎将成为周一在一级方程式委员会上讨论的关键议题，届时将辩论一项针对各队的“ADUO提案”。
正如《赛车》杂志首次报道的那样，威廉姆斯车队老板詹姆斯·沃尔斯提出了一个支出追赶机制的构想，以帮助一级方程式车队摆脱他认为已经成为‘成本上限陷阱’的困境。
沃尔斯认为，虽然成本上限规则在使所有车队在经济上具有可行性方面做得很好，但它也固化了既有的优势，这使得小车队难以赶上大型车队。
他正在推动在成本上限内实施一个滑动比例追赶系统，允许排名前四名之外的车队花费更多。
这意味着那些排名最后的车队将获得更大的财务自由，以帮助他们缩小与领先车队之间的差距。
Vowles的提议已被添加到下周F1委员会会议的议程中，正式命名为“ADUO for teams”。
这是指额外发展和升级机会，它存在于发动机制造商中 - 如果他们的动力单元低于基准，他们将获得额外的支出津贴、动力测试小时和认证机会。
Vowles最初希望为该计划获得足够的支持，以便它能够在明年尽早通过F1委员会并纳入规则手册。
为了实现这一点，需要国际汽联（FIA）、自由媒体公司（FOM）以及当前11支车队中的6支车队支持，这被称为超级多数支持。
但来自其他五支车队的支持似乎不太可能，目前只有凯迪拉克、阿尔派恩、阿斯顿·马丁和奥迪表示支持。
哈斯车队反对这一提议，因为它距离当前的成本上限还有一段距离，因此在支出上没有限制，而青训车队老板艾伦·帕尔曼表示他不支持这一概念。
然而，车队的分歧意见并不意味着这个想法已经死亡，因为总共四支车队的支持就足以让这个想法在2028年得以实施。
这将是足够早的，以便它能够帮助塑造2030年或2031年即将开始的下一个规则时代的形势。
沃尔斯最近表示，一个折中的解决方案仍然是可能的——特别是如果国际汽联和F1支持他的计划的话——但实施可能不会迅速。
“也许对我来说更重要的是，我有国际汽联和一级方程式的支持，”他说。
“我认为我们还没有一个足够准确的指导方向，我们需要采取的是正确的，对这项运动有益的方向，这仍然在幕后讨论中。”
“我能说的是，支持是存在的。”
““我认为这不会一夜之间发生。正如我之前提到的，我想要确保的是，我们在下一次规则变更之前把它做好，这个时间点还比较远，所以我们有足够的时间。”"
““但我的怀疑是，在接下来的几个月里，你将看到越来越多的讨论。”"
““但Vowles的想法并不是唯一受到关注的成本上限变化，因为这些讨论似乎将引发关于更广泛改革的争论。”"
F1的顶级车队从“ADUO车队”这一想法中获益甚少，因为最大的受益者将是那些希望关闭这些车队的车队。
但这并不意味着大型车队对当前成本上限规则的工作方式感到满意，因为他们也在寻求对规则的改变——以帮助F1保持竞争力。
其中最热门的话题之一是当前成本上限如何影响员工保留以及F1整体保持最优秀工程师的能力。
在成本上限下运营的车队被迫控制薪资，这导致许多F1车队在与那些被科技公司高薪吸引的才华横溢的人员争夺中处于劣势。
也有许多关于员工在其他赛车系列（除了F1）中能够赚取更多收入的例子，因为成本上限已经对工资设定了上限。
在全球生活成本危机的背景下，这个问题的重要性日益增加，因为F1的成本上限与通货膨胀紧密相连，所以车队无法提高工资以满足员工的需求。
现在正在逐渐形成的一个强有力的论点是，成本上限应该演变并区分零部件支出和人员支出。
正如F1规则长期以来所做的那样，只有组织内部薪酬最高的三名人员可以免除包含在成本上限内。
过去曾讨论过将人数扩展到最多300人，但人们认为这会是一个过于宽泛的范围，实际上会使成本上限失效。
在上周末的巴西大奖赛上，梅赛德斯车队老板托托·沃尔夫表示，他的车队早已提出了一个缓解机制——但这一提议被否决了。
他对天空体育说：“我本希望得到一点提升。我们提出的想法是，随着更多青训车队人员加入车队，我们将有更多的资金来支付他们更好的薪水，而不是在最初的五到七年内压低薪水。
“因此，我们向国际汽联提出了一个请求，希望给予我们一些补贴，不是更多的前翼补贴，而是希望薪水能稍微提高一些，因为成本上限压制了所有这些。但显然这并没有赢得很多好评。”
detailEn: Sweeping changes to cost cap rules look set to become a key area of discussion on Monday when an “ADUO for teams” proposal is debated at the Formula 1 Commission.
As first revealed by The Race, Williams team boss James Vowles has tabled the idea of a spending catch-up mechanism to help F1 teams escape what he thinks has become a “cost cap trap”.

Vowles argues that while the cost cap has done a great job making all teams financially viable, it has also locked in legacy advantages that make it difficult for smaller teams to catch up with the bigger squads.
He is pushing for a sliding scale catch-up system within the cost cap that allows the teams outside of the top four to spend more.
It would mean those teams that finish bottom of the standings get greater financial freedom to help them close the gap to squads at the front.
Vowles’ proposal has been added to the agenda of next week’s F1 Commission meeting, with it becoming formally known as “ADUO for teams”.

This is in reference to the ADUO (Additional Development and Upgrade Opportunities) that exists for engine manufacturers - who are given extra spending allowances, dyno hours and homologation opportunities if their power unit is adrift of the benchmark.
Vowles had originally hoped to get enough backing for the plan for it to get voted through the F1 Commission and into the rulebook as early as next year.
For that to happen, it would have required support from the FIA, FOM plus six of the current 11 teams for what is known as a supermajority.
But backing from five others appears unlikely, with only Cadillac, Alpine, Aston Martin and Audi supportive so far.
Haas is against because it is not near the current cost cap limit so is not limited on spending, while Racing Bulls team boss Alan Permane has said he does not back the concept.
The divided opinion in the paddock does not mean that the idea is dead, though, as support from four teams in total would be enough to get it into play for 2028.
That would be early enough for it to then help shape things for the next rules era that is due to start in 2030 or 2031.
Vowles said recently that a compromise solution remained possible - especially with support from the FIA and F1 over his plans - but implementation may not be swift.
“What's more important to me, perhaps, is I have the support of the FIA and Formula 1 behind it,” he said.
“I don't think we have an accurate enough direction that we need to take it in, that is right for the sport, which is still being discussed behind the scenes.
“What I can say is the support is there.

“I don't think it's going to happen overnight. As I previously mentioned, what I want to make sure is that we get it right by the next regulation change, which is a little way off, so we have some time.
“But my suspicion on it is you'll see more and more being discussed over the next few months in that regard.”
But Vowles’ idea is not the only cost cap change that is under the spotlight, because these discussions look set to trigger arguments about wider reform.
F1’s top teams have little to gain from the idea of an “ADUO for teams”, as the biggest beneficiaries would be those squads hoping to close them down.
But that does not mean the big squads are satisfied with how the current cost cap rules work, as they too are seeking changes to the regulations - to help F1 stay competitive.
One of the hottest topics among them is the way that current cost cap limits are impacting the retention of staff and the ability of F1 as a whole to keep hold of the brightest engineers.

Teams operating under the cost cap are forced to keep a lid on salaries, and that has left many F1 teams fighting a losing battle to retain talented personnel who are getting lured away by big-money offers from tech companies.
There are also many stories of staff being able to earn better money in other racing series outside of F1 because the cost cap has put a ceiling on wages so much.
The issue has increased in importance amid a global cost-of-living crisis, with F1’s cost cap increase tightly linked to inflation so teams are unable to lift salaries to respond to what staff need.
A strong argument that is now gathering some pace is for the cost cap to evolve and separate spending on parts and spending on people.
As has long been the case with F1’s rules, only the three highest-paid personnel within an organisation are exempt from being included within the cost cap.
There were discussions in the past about expanding this to include up to 300 staff, but it is thought that this would be too wide a net and would effectively make the cost cap ineffective.
Speaking at the Brazilian Grand Prix last weekend, Mercedes boss Toto Wolff said that his squad had long proposed a mitigating mechanism - but this was shot down.

He told Sky F1: “I would have loved to have a little bit of an uplift. The idea that we had was that with more junior personnel that joined the team, we would have more allowance to pay them better and not [having] the salaries suppressed in the first five, six, seven years.

“So we've pitched that to the FIA to give us an allowance, not for more front wings but an allowance for salaries to come up a little bit because the cost cap suppresses all of that. But obviously that didn't score a lot of brownie points.”
keyPointsZh: 威廉姆斯车队老板詹姆斯·沃尔斯提出了一项新的成本追赶机制。
沃尔斯认为成本上限虽然使所有车队在经济上可行，但也固化了传统优势，使小车队难以追赶大车队。
该计划旨在让排名靠后的车队获得更多财务自由，以缩小与领先车队的差距。
keyPointsEn: James Vowles has proposed a new spending catch-up mechanism.
Vowles believes that the cost cap has done a great job making all teams financially viable, but it has also locked in legacy advantages.
The plan aims to give teams at the bottom of the standings greater financial freedom to close the gap to the front-runners.

relatedItems.titleZh: 马德里F1赛事是否提升了经济价值？
relatedItems.summaryZh: 马德里马德里赛道首届2026年西班牙F1大奖赛创造了5.44亿欧元的产值，支持了10948个工作岗位，并产生了9500万欧元的税收。马德里赛道是一个部分街道赛道，位于IFEMA会议中心周围，赛道布局将在2027年进行更改，以提高比赛的品质和超车的频率。
relatedItems.originalTitle: Was Madrid F1 race an economic upgrade on Barcelona?
detailZh: 2026年首届马德里赛道西班牙一级方程式大奖赛创造了5.44亿欧元的产值，支持了10,948个就业岗位，并为税收贡献了9500万欧元，据主办方透露。
马德里赛道是一部分街道赛道，围绕着IFEMA会议中心建造，赛道布局将在2027年进行调整，以提高比赛的品质和超车的频率。
大奖赛推广商进行了一项由普华永道（PwC）进行的调查，显示与活动直接相关的每1欧元的经济活动，在马德里更广泛的经济中产生了4.60欧元的收益。
总经济影响比预期高出16.5%，大奖赛支持的就业岗位比预期多23.7%，总体税收贡献比预测多14.5%。
与马德里2026年的54.4亿欧元经济活动相比，巴塞罗那大奖赛在2024年为其当地经济活动产生了超过3亿欧元的收益，据其自身报告显示。巴塞罗那赛道首席执行官波尔·吉尔伯特在最近赛道扩建公告中重申了这一点，他表示“一级方程式在每个赛事中为场地产生了超过3亿欧元的经济效益。”
一级方程式首席执行官斯蒂法诺·多门卡利最近表示，奥斯汀的美国大奖赛在2026年为当地地区产生了“超过10亿美元”的收入，而拉斯维加斯大奖赛在其三届赛事中累计为当地地区产生了超过32亿美元的收入。
马德里国际展览中心（IFEMA）主席何塞·维森特·德·洛斯·莫索斯表示，这些数据“证实了大奖赛自首届以来为马德里经济和国际形象带来的战略重要性，其产生的经济活动相当于马德里地区GDP的0.16%和马德里市GDP的0.30%。”
大奖赛吸引了353,000名观众。调查显示，35%的游客来自海外，20%来自西班牙其他地区——这意味着45%的游客来自马德里及其周边地区。
国际游客在其停留期间的人均花费为2,772欧元 - 与西班牙游客的1,099欧元和马德里居民的659欧元相比 - 这些数字包括估计的平均票价，但票价并未公布。
因此，大奖赛的国际游客花费是马德里平均国际游客的1.7倍，是访问西班牙的国际游客的2.9倍。国内游客在马德里地区的旅行中花费是国内游客的3.8倍。
当地数字出版物《Democrata》发现，大奖赛期间酒店价格平均为485欧元 - 比平时高出70%。
大约49%的游客住在酒店，32%住在短期租赁住宿，19%与家人和朋友同住 - 产生了9,500万欧元的税收。
近年来，短期租赁一直是当地的一个有争议的问题，因为2025年，西班牙政府打击Airbnb，在全国范围内删除了近66,000个房源，并对该公司非法房源罚款6400万欧元。
此外，马德里赛道的当地居民抗议了其对环境和社会的负面影响，包括噪音问题。
调查发现，95.3%的国际与会者表示大奖赛‘提升了马德里在国际上的形象’，98.1%的人会推荐马德里作为旅游目的地，86%的与会者表示他们可能会再次回来。
普华永道合伙人Jordi Esteve表示：“通过广泛的实地调查，我们发现大奖赛的游客比普通游客花费更多，停留时间更长。这有助于马德里吸引高价值旅游，产生更大的经济活动并支持就业。”
普华永道在比赛周末的周五至周日之间进行了1,102次面对面调查。
detailEn: The inaugural 2026 Spanish Formula 1 Grand Prix at the Madring created €544 million in economic activity, supported 10,948 jobs, and generated €95m in tax revenue, according to its organiser.
The Madring is a part-street circuit built around the IFEMA conference centre - with the track layout set to be changed for 2027 to improve the quality of racing and frequency of overtaking.
The grand prix promoter ran a study conducted by PwC showing that, for every €1 of economic activity directly linked to the event, €4.60 was generated across Madrid’s wider economy.
The total economic impact was 16.5% larger than expected, the grand prix supported 23.7% more jobs than anticipated, and the overall tax contribution was 14.5% more than predicted.

In comparison to Madrid’s figure of €544m in economic activity for 2026, the Barcelona GP generated over €300m in local economic activity in 2024, according to its own reports. This was reaffirmed by Barcelona circuit CEO Pol Gilbert as part of the track’s recent extension announcement, where he said that “Formula 1 generates an economic impact of more than €300 million per edition” at the venue.

F1 CEO Stefano Domenicali recently said the US GP at Austin generated “over $1 billion” for the local area in 2026, while the Las Vegas GP has generated over $3.2bn cumulatively for the local area over its three editions.

IFEMA Madrid chairman Jose Vicente de los Mozos said that the figures “confirm the strategic importance the Grand Prix has gained for Madrid’s economy and international profile from its very first edition, generating economic activity equivalent to 0.16% of the Madrid Region’s GDP and 0.30% of the city of Madrid’s GDP”.

The grand prix attracted 353,000 attendees. The survey estimates that 35% of visitors were from overseas and 20% travelling from elsewhere in Spain - meaning 45% were from Madrid and its immediate vicinity.

International visitors spent an average of €2,772 per person over the course of their stay - compared with €1,099 from Spanish visitors and €659 among Madrid residents - with those figures including the estimated average ticket price, which is not stated.

International visitors to the grand prix therefore spent 1.7 times that of an average international tourist to Madrid, and 2.9 times more than an international tourist visiting Spain. Domestic visitors spent 3.8 times more than a domestic tourist would on a trip to the Madrid region.
Local digital publication Democrata found that hotel prices averaged €485 - 70% more than usual - for the grand prix.
Around 49% of visitors stayed in hotels, 32% in short-term rental accommodation, and 19% with family and friends - generating €95m in tax revenues.

Short-term rentals have been a contentious issue for the local area in recent years as, in 2025, the Spanish government cracked down on Airbnbs, removing nearly 66,000 listings across the country and fining the company €64m for illegal listings.
Furthermore, residents local to the Madring protested its environmental and societal impact, including noise concerns.

The survey found that 95.3% of international attendees said the grand prix had ‘enhanced Madrid’s international image’ and 98.1% would recommend Madrid as a tourist destination, with 86% of attendees saying they were likely to return.

PwC partner Jordi Esteve said: “Through extensive fieldwork, we have found that grand prix visitors spend more and stay longer than the average visitor. This is helping Madrid attract high-value tourism, generating greater economic activity and supporting employment.”
PwC conducted 1,102 face-to-face surveys between the Friday and Sunday of the race weekend.

relatedItems.titleZh: 法拉利勒克莱尔与汉密尔顿的矛盾远未解决
relatedItems.summaryZh: 法拉利车手勒克莱尔与汉密尔顿在巴西站期间经车队领队瓦塞尔调解后表面和睦，但文章认为两人之间的紧张关系远未真正解决。

media.altZh: 法拉利勒克莱尔与汉密尔顿的矛盾远未解决 · 第 1 张

relatedItems.originalTitle: Ferrari's Leclerc-Hamilton problem is far from solved
relatedItems.summaryEn: Ferrari drivers Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton appeared cordial in Brazil after mediation by team principal Fred Vasseur, but The Race argues the underlying tensions between them are far from resolved.
detailZh: 别被法拉利F1车手在巴西的和睦表现所迷惑；查尔斯·勒克莱尔与刘易斯·汉密尔顿之间仍然存在非常真实的紧张关系。
在汉密尔顿于墨西哥站因碰撞错失胜利后对勒克莱尔提出非同寻常的批评之后，两位车手与车队领队弗雷德·瓦塞尔在巴西聚在一起试图沟通解决问题。
那次会议被证明是有建设性的，勒克莱尔和汉密尔顿在巴西大奖赛期间表现得非常规矩，甚至遵守了车队指令并给彼此留出了充足的空间，与墨西哥站不同。
汉密尔顿的总结是：“一切都好。弗雷德把我们聚到一起。弗雷德在会议上很棒。然后他就让我和查尔斯各自表达观点。”
“我们双方进行了一次非常好、非常坦诚的讨论。现在一切都好了。我们只需继续向前。”
但墨西哥和巴西的情况不能相提并论，因此瓦塞尔没有费心去寻求那种本可轻易得到的赞许。
“这两种情况无法比较，”瓦塞尔在谈到勒克莱尔和汉密尔顿在英特拉格斯赛道上表现出的友好时说道。
“老实说，我们在周五进行了一次很好的讨论。我们把情况说清楚了。我们在心态上做了一次很好的调整。
“他们一起开着玩笑离开了我的房间。这很好。我希望这能持续下去，保持这样。”
瓦塞尔目前能做的只有“希望”这能持续下去，因为巴西那场争斗只可能是在积分区靠后的位置上展开，而不是争夺分站冠军或领奖台。
所以完全有理由相信，当法拉利赛车重新具备争胜实力时——无论是在拉斯维加斯、卡塔尔还是阿布扎比——汉密尔顿和勒克莱尔都会重新拼尽全力地较量。
毕竟，勒克莱尔在会后承认：“当然会有紧张气氛，当然我们都想跑在对方前面，有时我们也会做错事，有时在对事情的看法上存在分歧也没关系。”
“但与此同时，讨论这些内容会有很大帮助。”
鉴于勒克莱尔与汉密尔顿之间的紧张关系，勒克莱尔在法拉利的前队友卡洛斯·塞恩斯被问及他与勒克莱尔共事的那段时光。
毕竟，汉密尔顿曾指出勒克莱尔与塞恩斯和塞巴斯蒂安·维特尔共事的经历，以此作为他对队友竞争更激烈的证据。
“我对与查尔斯共事的时光以及我们之间的较量有着相对美好的回忆，”塞恩斯在巴西说道。
"确实，当你在为胜利而战时，压力总是更大，后续的事情也更多。所以你会自然而然地比在中游为第八或第九名而战时更自私一些。"
"也许更难完全遵循车队希望你遵循的理想情况，因为前方有胜利在望。当时前方也有胜利，但我一直尊重查尔斯。他也一直尊重我。我们从未有过接触或类似的事情。我们只是有过激烈的争斗。你还记得蒙扎、拉斯维加斯。那一年有很多激烈的时刻。"
"更困难的是车迷群体。当时公关和车迷群体真的被点燃了，在查尔斯和我之间非常两极分化。我记得有点受到查尔斯非常铁杆车迷的辱骂或诅咒的困扰。"
"也许一些意大利媒体也说我在需要的时候不够二号车手，反之亦然，每当查尔斯不得不这样做的时候。"
所以，更多的是围绕法拉利的压力，涉及法拉利，而不是我和查尔斯之间实际存在的问题，那些问题总是在当晚我们用更冷静的头脑互相打电话时就解决了，我们总能找到解决方案和前进的方向。
塞恩斯觉得，同一支车队里有两个平等的车手，这是一个不可避免的问题。
“我不记得有哪支一级方程式车队拥有两位优秀车手在前方争夺，却在为胜利而战时没有出现过问题，”塞恩斯补充道。
“你可以选择让一位二号车手担任第二车手，或者你可以拥有两位优秀车手，而他们会制造那些问题。但在我看来，你不能只要其一而不要其二。而且你永远不可能只要其一而不要其二。
“也许在法拉利，涉及法拉利的一切会让情况变得有些加剧，但我想不起有哪一刻没发生过这种事。梅赛德斯发生过。过去几年迈凯伦发生过。法拉利也发生过。”
“所以我不知道什么时候没发生过。这是F1的一部分。如果你是车队领队，而且你知道自己将拥有两位伟大的车手，你就总会遇到这个问题。”
“我不认为你能让那两个人百分之百冷静下来，还指望他们不为分站冠军发起进攻。”
这与2019年的紧张局势有某些相似之处，当时勒克莱尔以21岁的年纪成功从四届世界冠军维特尔手中夺走了法拉利的头号地位。Mark Hughes的这篇文章至今仍是关于那段往事的出色记述。
那时，车手们可以自由竞争，车队领队（马蒂亚·比诺托）试图公平行事，车手们在表现上足够接近，经常在赛道上彼此靠近，并且有一场激烈的霸权争夺战。
勒克莱尔最终令人信服地赢得了那场战斗，塞恩斯被引入以取代维特尔，但从未与勒克莱尔平起平坐。（这也不意味着他是一个尽职的二号车手。他太快了，不适合那样。）
勒克莱尔和塞恩斯有过摩擦点，但最终事情从未失控地爆发，原因很简单：大约三分之二的时间里，勒克莱尔都领先于塞恩斯。
因此，动态非常不同：勒克莱尔甚至最终帮助塞恩斯在2023年新加坡站取得了唯一一场非维斯塔潘的胜利。这证明了勒克莱尔在放长线钓大鱼，他知道在那里做出小小的牺牲只会在他一旦拥有法拉利争冠赛车时加强他的地位。
最终，两人之间的性能差距足够大，因此从未产生过太多针锋相对。勒克莱尔并不把塞恩斯视为对自己法拉利领军地位的威胁。他是对的，因为在那场新加坡胜利仅几个月后，法拉利就选择用汉密尔顿取代了塞恩斯。
而在2025年，勒克莱尔与汉密尔顿之间存在明显的性能差距，这意味着两人之间没有太多针锋相对，这并非巧合。
突然间，他们在2026年实力非常接近，勒克莱尔-维特尔时代的紧张关系立刻重新暴露出来，因为现在勒克莱尔的位置受到了威胁。勒克莱尔此前相当从容，就像维特尔在2015-18年作为车队核心时那样，队友基米·莱科宁很大程度上只是辅助角色。
现在，队内主导权之争已经打响。如果法拉利明年改进其动力单元并拥有争冠赛车，汉密尔顿和勒克莱尔都希望成为引领车队冲锋的那个人。
这就是为什么认为法拉利在巴西的会议能给勒克莱尔与汉密尔顿之间的问题画上句号的想法纯属无稽之谈。
这种情况不会改变，直到勒克莱尔像当年击败维特尔那样再次击溃另一位世界冠军，或者直到他自己被队友击溃。
detailEn: Don't be fooled by Ferrari's Formula 1 drivers playing nicely in Brazil; there are still very real tensions between Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton.
The drivers and team principal Fred Vasseur got together in Brazil to try to talk things through after Hamilton's extraordinary criticism of Leclerc following their victory-losing Mexico run-in.
That meeting proved constructive, and Leclerc and Hamilton were very well-behaved during the Brazilian Grand Prix, even following team orders and leaving each other plenty of room, unlike in Mexico.
Hamilton's summary was: "Everything's good. Fred brought us together. Fred was great in the meeting. And then he just left me and Charles to just give our points.
"We both had a really good, open discussion. And it's all good now. We'll just move on."
But you can't compare Mexico and Brazil, so Vasseur didn't bother reaching for what would have been an easy pat-on-the-back.
"You can't compare the two situations," Vasseur said, in respect of Leclerc and Hamilton's cordiality on-track at Interlagos.
"Honestly, we had a good discussion on Friday. We cleared the situation. We did a good reset on the mindset.
"They left my room joking together. It's good. I hope that it will last, to stay like this."
All Vasseur can do for now is "hope" it lasts because that Brazil fight was only ever going to be for minor points-paying positions, not a race win or a podium.
So there's every reason to believe that when the Ferrari is back fighting for wins, be it in Las Vegas or Qatar or Abu Dhabi, Hamilton and Leclerc are going to be back fighting tooth and nail.

After all, Leclerc admitted post-meeting: "Of course there is tension, of course we want to finish ahead of each other, and sometimes we are not going to do things right, and it's OK sometimes to disagree on the way you see things.
"But at the same time discussing about those helps a whole lot."
In light of the Leclerc-Hamilton tensions, Leclerc's ex-team-mate at Ferrari Carlos Sainz was asked about his time with Leclerc.
Hamilton had, after all, pointed to Leclerc's time alongside Sainz and Sebastian Vettel as evidence that he races his team-mates harder.
"I have relatively good memories of my time with Charles and the fights we had," Sainz said in Brazil.

"It is true that when you're fighting for wins, there's always more pressure, more things down the line. So you become naturally a bit more selfish than when you are fighting in the midfield for a P8 or a P9.

"It's more difficult maybe to follow exactly the ideal situation that the team would like you to follow, because there's a win down the line. There was wins down the line back then, but I always respected Charles. He always respected me. We never had contacts or anything like this. We just had strong fights. You remember Monza, Vegas. There was plenty of hot moments during the year.

"What was difficult more was the fanbase. The PR and the fanbase was really ignited back then, and it was very polarised between Charles and me. And I remember suffering a bit from the very hardcore fans of Charles insulting or wishing me bad.
"Maybe some Italian media also saying that I was not being enough of a number two when I needed to be, and vice-versa whenever Charles had to do it.

"So it's more the pressure surrounding Ferrari, that involves Ferrari, than the actual issues that I had with Charles, which were always resolved that same night when we called each other with a more cold head and we always managed to find the solution and the way forward."
Sainz felt it is an inevitable problem with having two equals in the same team.
"I cannot remember no Formula 1 team that has had two good drivers fighting at the front that haven't had issues when fighting for wins," Sainz added.

"You can choose whether to have a number two as a second driver, or you can have two good drivers that will create those issues. But you cannot have one without the other, in my opinion. And you will never have one without the other.

"Maybe in Ferrari it gets a bit exacerbated with everything that involves Ferrari, but I cannot remember a moment where this hasn't happened. It happened in Mercedes. It happened in McLaren the last few years. It happened in Ferrari.
"So I don’t know when it hasn't happened. It is part of Formula 1. And if you are a team principal and you know you're going to have two great drivers, you're always going to have that issue.
"I don't think you can ever calm those two guys 100% down and expect them not to go for a move for a race win."

There are some parallels to the tensions in 2019 when Leclerc managed to steal Ferrari away from four-time world champion Sebastian Vettel as a 21-year-old. This piece by Mark Hughes still stands as an excellent account of that.

Back then, the drivers were 'free to race', the team principal (Mattia Binotto) tried to play things fairly, the drivers were close enough in performance to routinely be near each other on track, and there was a huge battle for supremacy.

Leclerc ultimately won that battle convincingly, with Sainz brought into replace Vettel, but never as an equal to Leclerc. (That didn't mean he was a dutiful number two either. He was too quick for that.)
Leclerc and Sainz had their flashpoints, but ultimately things never uncontrollably spilt over for one good reason: Leclerc was ahead of Sainz around two-thirds of the time.

The dynamic therefore was very different: Leclerc even ended up helping Sainz to the only non-Verstappen victory of 2023 in Singapore. That was evidence of Leclerc playing the long game, knowing a small sacrifice there would only strengthen his position once Ferrari had a title-challenging car.

There was ultimately enough of a performance gap for there never to be too much needle between them. Leclerc didn't see Sainz as a threat to his position as Ferrari's spearhead. He was right, as Ferrari chose to replace Sainz with Hamilton just a few months after that Singapore win.
And it's no coincidence that in 2025, there being a clear performance gap between Leclerc and Hamilton meant there wasn't much needle between them.

Suddenly they're very closely matched in 2026, and the Leclerc-Vettel era tension is immediately re-exposed because now there is a threat to Leclerc's position. Leclerc was previously fairly comfortable, like Vettel was in 2015-18 as the focal point of the team, with team-mate Kimi Raikkonen very much a support act.
Now there is an active battle for supremacy. If Ferrari improves its power unit and has a title-challenging car next year, both Hamilton and Leclerc want to be the one leading that charge.
It's why the prospect of Ferrari's Brazil meeting being any kind of full stop on its Leclerc-Hamilton problem is absolute nonsense.
That's not going to change until Leclerc has destroyed another world champion - as he did to Vettel - or until he's the one destroyed by a team-mate.

瓦塞尔只能希望这种和睦能持续，因为巴西站的争夺仅涉及积分区靠后的位置，而非胜利或领奖台。
keyPointsEn: Hamilton made extraordinary criticism of Leclerc after their victory-losing Mexico run-in.
Vasseur said the two had a good discussion on Friday, cleared the situation and reset their mindset, leaving his room joking together.
Vasseur can only hope the cordiality lasts, as the Brazil fight was only for minor points-paying positions, not a win or podium.
